conventions: spine-wire v1 conformance vectors. Generated by scripts/wire_v1.py from docs/spec/00-wire.md; do not edit by hand.
Regenerate: python scripts/wire_v1.py generate > docs/spec/00-wire.vectors.json. Check: python scripts/wire_v1.py check docs/spec/00-wire.vectors.json.
All 'hex' strings are lowercase, no spaces or prefix. A frame is u32 length, u8 version, u8 type, u8 flags, u64 request id (all big-endian), then the body.
Value descriptions: a JSON object is a CBOR map with text keys; arrays, strings, true, false and null are as in JSON.
A JSON number with a '.' or an exponent is a CBOR float; any other JSON number is a CBOR integer.
{"$bytes": "<hex>"} is a CBOR byte string. {"$int": "<decimal>"} is an integer beyond +-2^53 (JSON numbers are inexact there).
{"$float": "nan"|"inf"|"-inf"} is a float JSON cannot write. {"$map": [[key, value], ...]} is a map whose keys are not all text.
valid_bodies: deterministic CBOR items a decoder must accept. 'hex' is the exact encoding; 'value' describes it.
invalid_bodies: items a decoder must reject. 'reason' is the Rust cbor::CborError variant name, which is also the rule broken (C.5).

valid_frames: whole frames. 'type', 'request_id', 'flags' and 'body' (or 'body_hex') describe 'hex'. 'typed' names the body type that decodes it: command, reply, ping, pong, stream, hello, hello_ack, close, ext, or none (decode and re-encode of the typed value is not offered, e.g. a result with byte strings).

A frame with flags 1 has the body u32 uncompressed_len, then a zstd frame. These vectors store the body in a raw-block zstd frame (valid zstd, not smaller). A receiver must decode them to 'body_hex'; they are not byte-for-byte what a compressing sender would emit, so re-encoding is not part of the check.

invalid_frames: whole frames (or the prefix needed to decide) that a receiver using 'max_frame' as the maximum in force must reject with 'error' (the Rust frame::FrameError variant) and 'close_code' (C.7 wire text). 'build' re-derives 'hex'. incomplete_frames: valid prefixes; 'needed' is the least number of further bytes (FrameError::NeedMore).
The order of the stateless frame checks is: length, version, type, flags, request id, then the body (specification section 7.2).

handshakes: 'hello_frame' is a whole HELLO frame, 'local' the server configuration, 'expect' the outcome of validating the HELLO and negotiating: an 'ack' (with the whole 'ack_frame') or a 'close' with its code and 'supported'. CLOSE 'message' text is not specified and not part of a vector.
A vector with a 'note' explains the rule it exercises and cites the section of docs/spec/00-wire.md that states it.
Not covered: connection state (id reuse, direction, HELLO first, extension index, timeouts, max_inflight) and real zstd compression.

valid_bodies.name: nan_is_f97e00
valid_bodies.note: NaN of any payload or sign is written as f9 7e 00 (section 5 rule 2)

valid_bodies.name: keys_by_first_byte

valid_bodies.name: keys_mixed_types

valid_bodies.name: depth_32_arrays_empty_innermost
valid_bodies.note: 32 nested arrays; the innermost is empty. Accepted.

valid_bodies.name: depth_32_arrays_with_scalar
valid_bodies.note: 32 nested arrays around a scalar. Accepted: scalars do not count.

valid_bodies.name: depth_32_mixed
valid_bodies.note: alternating arrays and maps, 32 levels, the innermost an empty array. Accepted.

valid_frames.name: hello_ack_extensions_and_agent

valid_frames.name: pong_with_id_zero

valid_frames.name: request_optional_absent_resolve_name

valid_frames.name: request_tool_call_nested_json_arguments
valid_frames.note: integers keep their integer type, floats the shortest width (section 5 rule 2); no NaN or infinity: a JSON-shaped value cannot hold them

valid_frames.name: response_with_id_zero
valid_frames.note: the frame layer accepts id 0 on a RESPONSE; the connection layer rejects it because no request is in flight (section 8.1)

valid_frames.name: response_ok_byte_string

valid_frames.name: stream_cancel_empty
